asr.full_text: Hey this is Tom and my video show you how to buy and sell coins and to purchase tokens go down to your Exchange which is right here you wonder in the exchange you can go into trading. And if you want to buy tokens, you simply click here on Bid. You want to sell your coins, you click here on Ask. Okay so let's go ahead and say we're going to buy, I had clicked on how many coins you have So I'll just make a simple example I want to buy one coin so I put in there and it deducted the money I didn't have any money left over from all of the gift codes. Then you come in here and you come in here and put in your Transaction Password and you hit Place Order. A minimum order of ten coins, so I can't do anything right now in this particular account. So, that is how you would buy coins. If you're interested in selling coins let me close this out. You would come on Ask and you would come in to ask and you can go in and sell the coins now notice I was buying them at $1.45 a piece and if I want to sell 10 coins I simply go in here and I put in 10 coins it says transaction value 14 dollars and 50 cents 25 cent transaction fee I type in my password and I hit place order and they put the money into my Cash account. So that is how you buy coins and sell coins. Okay, so let me go in and show you how to do mining. If you have tokens in your account, you click on mining and right now you can see I have 10000 638 coins in this account have a hundred and sixty-four thousand tokens in mining right now on this particular account if I had I extra tokens which I do not right now a simply would come down here and put in 10,000 tokens are whatever and hit submit and then confirm it in I would and it would tell me what my exchange rate is. So I can go to accounts like I want to see what my values are I can go to token, account, and I can see the ratio at which I am mining. So if I go to my second page. You can see I have 60,000 coins I mined at six tokens per coin. Okay, that's how I got the 10,000 coins on this account. And so let's go to the next page. Now you can see I got 9, 657 in and that went into a difficulty rate of 10 coins 10 tokens per coin so that'll get me what 100 coins or a thousand coins on this particular purchase and then another two thousand went in for my mandatory account and then of course there was our split $360,000, and those tokens went into a mining operation at 12 tokens per Coin. Then, of course, I had another $180,000 come into my account, and those have been submitted for mining, as well. This allows you to keep track of all the coins all the tokens that you have going into mining and the difficulty rate at which you're earning those coins ok so in this video I've shown you how to buy and buy the coins and I've shown you how to buy and sell the how to track how many tokens you have in the mining process in at what rates they're actually being my that so i hope this video helps you but simply again go to exchange and go into trading and if you want to buy coins, click on that. One is the coin, so that's how you would buy coins. Then it will show all your transactions over here that you've done. So there's tokens so you'll see all the tokens that I bought. Click on that again, takes you back to coins. So one is the coin, the other one is the tokens if you want to buy and sell the coins you want to sell them you're getting a dollar 45 if you want to buy them you're getting a dollar 55 and that is how you trade internally within our platform hope that makes sense thanks for your time

textual.observation: The source promotes using an internal platform to buy coins and tokens, submit a transaction password and payment order, and place tokens into mining at stated token-per-coin rates to obtain coins.

evidence.quote: If you have tokens in your account, you click on mining
You can see I have 60,000 coins I mined at six tokens per coin.
I type in my password and I hit place order and they put the money into my Cash account.

textual.context: The speaker presents a first-person instructional demonstration of buying, selling and mining on the platform; the supplied records do not establish whether the described outcomes are guaranteed or independently verified.
textual.potential_relevance: The requested purchase, password submission and token-mining steps are directly connected to obtaining or earning coins, with stated conversion rates and a description of profit; later review may assess the conditions and substantiation of that reward or return relationship.
textual.limitations: The records do not establish actual transaction completion, financial outcome, legitimacy of the platform, or whether the described mining rates and profit statement applied beyond the demonstrated account.

visual.observation: A visible buy-order form for One tokens requires account balances, shows a transaction value and a payment method referencing a mandatory account and cash account, and includes a "PLACE ORDER" control.
visual.context: Context is unclear; the frame shows an exchange interface with a buy-order form.
visual.potential_relevance: The interface links placing a token purchase order to a stated mandatory-account balance and cash-account payment condition, which is a concrete payment and account-action relationship.
visual.limitations: The sampled frame does not establish whether an audience was being instructed to use the form, whether any payment occurred, or whether the displayed account requirements were enforced.

visual.observation: The transaction-history interface displays multiple entries described as automatic buys from mandatory accounts, including token quantities and transaction-fee references; another entry shows a split bonus for crypto currency.
visual.context: Context is unclear; the frames show historical account transactions within a branded token-account interface.
visual.potential_relevance: The displayed history connects automatic token purchases and bonus-related entries with mandatory accounts and transaction fees, providing a concrete account and funds-flow mechanism that may merit review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish who initiated the transactions, whether the records are genuine, whether funds were transferred, or whether the video promotes, reports, or demonstrates this mechanism.

textual_context_notes.observation: The video is framed as a how-to guide for buying and selling OneCoins and tokens within an exchange.

textual_context_notes.observation: The demonstrated account includes explicit transaction conditions, including a minimum order and a transaction fee.

evidence.quote: A minimum order of ten coins

visual_context_notes.observation: The sampled frames show OneCoin-branded dashboard, exchange, mining, and transaction-history interfaces, including buy/sell controls, token price charts, and account summaries.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes participation in the OneCoin system by showing viewers how to place buy and sell orders, purchase tokens, and submit those tokens to a mining process that is presented as producing coins and profit. The speaker describes personal token purchases and mining balances, then directs viewers through the exchange and mining workflow, making this an active solicitation rather than neutral market commentary.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S04 fits because the video links purchased tokens and substantial account payments to recurring coin production through a mining operation. S05 is separately supported because the video also promotes buying and trading the platform's tokens while the description states that users can profit through the virtual-currency system.
